html:
The Namibian War of Independence was fought from 1966 to 1989 by SWAPO's guerrilla army against South African rule in South West Africa, mainly in the north and from bases in Angola and Zambia.

It began with a clash at Omugulugwombashe in August 1966. After Angola became independent in 1975, SWAPO fighters operated from there, and South Africa struck deep into Angola, fighting the Angolan civil war alongside UNITA against Angolan and Cuban forces. Ovamboland in the north bore the brunt, with curfews and abuses by the Koevoet police unit.

The stalemate at Cuito Cuanavale in 1988 led to agreements in which Cuban troops left Angola and South Africa left Namibia. Sam Nujoma led SWAPO to power at independence in 1990.
sum: The Namibian War of Independence was fought from 1966 to 1989 by SWAPO's guerrilla army against South African rule in South West Africa, mainly in the north and from bases in Angola and Zambia.
